---
title: "Weekly Ticket Volume"
description: "Number of PSOM tickets in each Monday snapshot."
---

The total number of PSOM tickets captured in each Monday snapshot, showing how
the number of tickets in the project changes over time.

## Calculation

Keep only the Monday `date` partitions and count the rows in
each. The snapshot ran weekly on Mondays until 2026-09-28 and nightly from
2026-09-29, so filtering to Mondays gives one comparable total per week across
the whole history.

For a finer view from 2026-09-29 on, count every partition: there is one per
night.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

By week:

```sql
SELECT
    date,
    COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
FROM jira.psom
WHERE day_of_week(CAST(date AS DATE)) = 1
GROUP BY date
ORDER BY date DESC;
```

By day, from the first nightly snapshot:

```sql
SELECT
    date,
    COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
FROM jira.psom
WHERE CAST(date AS DATE) >= DATE '2026-09-29'
GROUP BY date
ORDER BY date DESC;
```

## R

By week:

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("jira", "psom")) |>
  filter(wday(as.Date(date), week_start = 1) == 1) |>
  count(date, name = "ticket_count") |>
  arrange(desc(date))
```

By day, from the first nightly snapshot:

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("jira", "psom")) |>
  filter(as.Date(date) >= as.Date("2026-09-29")) |>
  count(date, name = "ticket_count") |>
  arrange(desc(date))
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

This counts the tickets still in the project on each
Monday, not the tickets opened that week or the open backlog; for those, see
[Tickets Opened, Closed, and Open](tickets-opened-closed-and-open.qmd). It includes
`Done` and `Canceled` tickets until they are archived, and it drops when a
batch of tickets is archived (from 52 to 25 between 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-21).
The first snapshot, 2026-06-30, was a Tuesday, so the filter leaves it out.

## Alternative names

- total tickets per week
- weekly PSOM ticket count
- ticket volume trend
